issues.failure_explanation: The proof only uses continuous embedding $\mathcal{B}_1\hookrightarrow H^1$ and compact embedding $H^1\hookrightarrow L^2$, which gives at most $L^2$-compactness of $\mathcal{B}_1$-bounded sequences, not $H^1$-compactness. The statement that every bounded $\mathcal{B}_1$ sequence has an $H^1$-convergent subsequence is false.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lemma with the correct $L^2$-compactness statement and supply a separate argument to upgrade convergence to $H^1$, or weaken the affected convergence claims to $L^2$.
issues.overall_effect: The $H^1$ convergence claims in Theorem main and in the $\mathcal{R}=\mathcal{R}_2$ case of Theorem main2 rely on this false lemma and are not established as written.

issues.why_classification: A central compactness tool is false, and the main $H^1$ regularization guarantees depend on it; repairing this requires new proof architecture or a substantive weakening of the advertised convergence.

issues.failure_explanation: For a concave sublinear index function such as $\Phi(t)=c_0 t^\mu$ with $0<\mu<1$, the Fenchel conjugate defined by $\sup_{t\ge0}(\alpha t-\Phi(t))$ is infinite for every $\alpha>0$, so $\Phi^{-*}$ is undefined. The Young inequality and the error estimate in Theorem convergencerate are therefore not justified as written.

failure_location.quote: $\Phi^{-*}$ denotes the (generalized) inverse of the Fenchel conjugate $\Phi^*$ of $\Phi$, defined by $\Phi^*(\alpha) := \sup_{t \ge 0} \{\alpha t - \Phi(t)\}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct Legendre-type transform for concave index functions (or restate the source condition with a convex index function) and prove the corresponding Young inequality.
issues.overall_effect: The error bound (i) and the convergence-rate proof in Theorem convergencerate, and the special rate in Corollary corollary1, are unsupported under the stated concavity assumption.
issues.title: Fenchel conjugate used for concave index function is ill-defined
issues.why_classification: The advertised rates can likely be recovered with a corrected convex-analysis tool, but the current proof uses an undefined object and needs a nontrivial correction.
